query_snapshot: According to NBS Circular 592, which molybdenum-bearing stainless-steel types were reported as most resistant to sulfuric acid at low temperatures, and what limitations prevent treating that statement as a universal material recommendation?
final_answer:
Evidence-grounded answer:

- NBS Circular 592 reports that molybdenum-bearing stainless-steel types 316 and 317 were the most resistant to sulfuric acid at low temperatures. [nbscircular592.pdf, pp. 59-60, chunk b0a15485; nbscircular592.pdf, p. 60, chunk 2b809bc1]
- The Circular states that at about 150°F all of the stainless steels corrode in practically all concentrations of sulfuric acid up to 95 percent. [nbscircular592.pdf, pp. 59-60, chunk b0a15485; nbscircular592.pdf, p. 60, chunk 2b809bc1]
- Roach and Hall reported that molybdenum-bearing stainless steels were useful, at room temperature, in concentrations of sulfuric acid below 15 percent and above 85 percent. [nbscircular592.pdf, pp. 59-60, chunk b0a15485; nbscircular592.pdf, p. 60, chunk 2b809bc1]
- The Circular states that resistance to sulfuric acid is improved in some cases by additions of copper or cerium. [nbscircular592.pdf, pp. 59-60, chunk b0a15485; nbscircular592.pdf, p. 60, chunk 2b809bc1]
- Halide ions (for example chlorides) attack the passive film on stainless steel and produce pitting corrosion; additions of molybdenum reduce the susceptibility to pitting corrosion. [nbscircular592.pdf, pp. 59-60, chunk b0a15485; nbscircular592.pdf, p. 60, chunk 2b809bc1]
- Stress-corrosion cracking severity depends on composition, corrosive medium, temperature, nature and extent of tensile stresses, and other factors; the Circular gives examples (e.g., boiling magnesium chloride produced cracks in hours while exposure to a glucose solution required 14 years). [nbscircular592.pdf, pp. 59-60, chunk b0a15485; nbscircular592.pdf, pp. 60-61, chunk e035b4b6]
- Because the Circular ties the 316/317 advantage to low temperatures and lists multiple temperature-, concentration-, environment-, and stress-dependent limits, it does not support treating the 316/317 statement as a universal material recommendation for sulfuric-acid service. [nbscircular592.pdf, pp. 59-60, chunk b0a15485; nbscircular592.pdf, p. 60, chunk 2b809bc1; nbscircular592.pdf, pp. 60-61, chunk e035b4b6]
